subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should externally or plugin-registered recurring `agentTurn` cron jobs require explicit operator activation and model/cost guardrails before they can run?
rationale: The source path is clear, but fixing it changes scheduler security boundaries, plugin scheduling API expectations, upgrade behavior, and provider quota policy.

options.title: Require explicit activation for external recurring agentTurn jobs
options.body: Preserve operator-authored cron behavior where appropriate, but make externally/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs carry trusted provenance, default disabled or pending, and require an explicit model or cost acknowledgment before running.

options.title: Keep enabled-by-default and document operator responsibility
options.body: Treat existing cron.add semantics as the compatibility contract and improve docs/doctor warnings without changing runtime activation behavior.

options.title: Split Into Existing Follow-Ups
options.body: Use the related quota, budget, and provenance issues for separate implementation and keep this issue as the consent/default-model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation for external recurring agentTurn jobs
recommendation.body: Preserve operator-authored cron behavior where appropriate, but make externally/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs carry trusted provenance, default disabled or pending, and require an explicit model or cost acknowledgment before running.
